title: Cozy cooking game with a twist
author: Raging_Rob
selftext:
Code and 3D models done mainly with Opus 5.5. 

My workflow for the modelling involves starting with some concept art until I find something I like and then generating reference images at different angles that Claude can use along with Blender.

I also use GPT Image for the textures and sprites. For example, sprite generation using AI has been super helpful for all the different NPC variations within the minigames. This involved over 60 unique sprites to support all the different characters in the game which would have taken me so long to do without AI and definitely would have looked worse.

comments.author: ZeusGameAssets
comments.body:
That's one of the worst ideas I've ever had and you just made it into an actual game. I'm not saying this to criticize, but to save you time and tokens if you want to take this into production.

Such a cozy aesthetic comes with a lot of expectations from players. Sourcing your meat from humans is very far from what players of such games would expect. My guess is most people would be put off by this, unless you match the aesthetic to your core idea, why not do it in a dark grungy abandoned church where your main customers are zombies, that would give the idea some commercial viability.

This is sick, and I like it, but my guess is the general public of players would skip your game because of it.

Also, get some therapy you sick bastard 😂.

replies.author: BridgeLazy5669
replies.body: That would kill the whole allure of OPs game, making it cozy but dark themed is exactly what makes it unique and actually interesting, I’d play OPs game at least out of curiosity, but I wouldn’t play dark themed gothic cooking game where you feed zombies, because it sounds like mobile game slop, whilst cozy cooking game where you make burgers out of humans sounds hilarious and fun, but I would expect it to be actually funny and comedic

replies.author: ZeusGameAssets
replies.body:
I've yet to see a successful game idea that targets a particular audience having the aesthetics of games that appeal to a completely different audience. I'm specifically talking about commercial viability and success.

Is the idea original and something I'd love to play? Yes, I don't dislike the deceptive nature of the cozy game aesthetic. However, for marketing, it's going to be very tough to sell this to the proper audience.
